## Dengue data

Here we will return to the dengue data from class. Our model is

$$Dengue_i \sim Bernoulli(\pi_i)$$
$$\log \left( \dfrac{\pi_i}{1 - \pi_i} \right) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 WBC_i$$

Here is the output for the fitted model from R:

```
Coefficients:
            Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
(Intercept)  1.73743    0.08499   20.44   <2e-16 ***
WBC         -0.36085    0.01243  -29.03   <2e-16 ***
```

1. Calculate a 99% confidence interval for the change in the log odds of dengue associated with a one-unit increase in WBC.

\vspace{1.5cm}

2. How could we calculate a 99% confidence interval for the change in the *odds* of dengue associated with a one-unit increase in WBC?

\vspace{1.5cm}

3. Your friend, seeing your confidence interval from question 2, states that there is a 1% chance that the true change in odds associated with a one-unit increase in WBC is less than 0.675 or greater than 0.720. Is your friend correct?
